description: Author the AWS CDK (TypeScript) infrastructure for one-command deploy and the README. Provisions DynamoDB table, Lambda functions (bundled from backend), API Gateway (HTTP API) with CORS, Bedrock InvokeModel IAM permissions, S3 bucket + CloudFront distribution for the SPA, and wiring so the frontend build is deployed and pointed at the API. Verified via `cdk synth` only (no deploy - AWS creds inactive). Depends on FEAT-002 (handlers) and FEAT-003 (frontend build output).
steps: Flesh out infra/package.json (name @mlb/infra) with aws-cdk-lib, constructs, and dev deps aws-cdk (CLI), typescript, ts-node, @types/node, esbuild (for NodejsFunction bundling). Scripts: build (tsc), synth (cdk synth), deploy (cdk deploy), bootstrap (cdk bootstrap), typecheck (tsc --noEmit). Add infra/cdk.json with app: `npx ts-node --prefer-ts-exts bin/app.ts`.
infra/bin/app.ts: CDK App instantiating the stack with env from CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT/REGION.

infra/lib/mlb-postseason-stack.ts: define resources: (1) DynamoDB Table (PAY_PER_REQUEST, partition key pk:string, TTL attribute) for bracket cache. (2) Two aws_lambda_nodejs.NodejsFunction constructs (Node 20 runtime) pointing at backend/src/handlers/getBracket.ts and getPrediction.ts, entry resolved relative to the backend workspace, with TABLE_NAME and BEDROCK_MODEL_ID env vars, memory/timeout sensible for a Bedrock call (e.g., 512MB / 30s on prediction). (3) Grant the table read/write to both functions. (4) Grant Bedrock InvokeModel via an iam.PolicyStatement (bedrock:InvokeModel on the Claude model ARNs / * for the region) to the prediction function. (5) HTTP API (aws_apigatewayv2) with routes GET /bracket -> getBracket, GET /prediction -> getPrediction (or POST), CORS allowing the CloudFront origin and localhost dev. (6) S3 bucket (private, OAC) for the SPA + CloudFront distribution with default root object index.html and SPA error-routing (403/404 -> /index.html). (7) BucketDeployment deploying frontend/dist to the bucket (with a note/mechanism to inject the API URL - e.g., deploy-time config.js or build-time env). (8) CfnOutputs: ApiUrl, DistributionDomainName, BucketName, TableName.

Handle the frontend API URL wiring: document and implement a workable approach - e.g., a BucketDeployment that also writes a config.js with window.__API_BASE_URL__, and frontend/src/config.ts reads that at runtime (falling back to VITE_API_BASE_URL). Keep it simple and documented in README.
Add infra/.gitignore entries for cdk.out (or rely on root .gitignore).

Ensure `npm run build -w infra` (tsc) and `npm run synth -w infra` (cdk synth) succeed and produce a CloudFormation template in cdk.out. If NodejsFunction bundling via esbuild requires network/docker, prefer esbuild (no docker). If synth cannot bundle without building backend first, wire the root build order so backend is built before synth, and document it.

Write README.md at repo root: project overview; architecture diagram (ASCII or described); the MLB data strategy (MLB Stats API + DynamoDB cache + seed fallback); Bedrock usage; prerequisites (Node 20+, AWS account, Bedrock model access enabled in the region); ONE-COMMAND deploy: `npm install && npm run build && npm run deploy` (where root deploy runs cdk bootstrap if needed then cdk deploy), plus explicit `cd infra && npx cdk bootstrap && npx cdk deploy` steps; local dev instructions (`npm run dev -w frontend`, how to point at a deployed API or run against seed data); how steering files map to Kiro University lessons; and a clear note that AWS credentials must be active and Bedrock model access granted before deploy. Note the image-asset approach (committed SVGs).
Make the root `npm run build` build order: shared -> backend -> frontend -> infra, and `npm run synth`/`deploy` depend on build.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build -w infra` compiles the CDK app with no TypeScript errors.
`npm run synth -w infra` (cdk synth) produces a CloudFormation template in cdk.out without errors (no deploy performed).

The stack defines DynamoDB, two Lambda functions, an HTTP API with CORS, Bedrock InvokeModel IAM permission on the prediction function, and S3 + CloudFront for the SPA, with CfnOutputs for ApiUrl and the CloudFront domain.

README.md documents a one-command deploy (npm install && npm run build && npm run deploy) plus explicit cdk bootstrap/deploy, local dev, data strategy, Bedrock prerequisites, and the Kiro University mapping.
Root `npm run build` builds all workspaces in dependency order and the whole repo typechecks.
verification: From repo root: `npm run build` exits 0 (shared, backend, frontend, infra all build).
From repo root: `npm run synth` (cdk synth) exits 0 and writes cdk.out with a template.
Confirm README.md contains the one-command deploy instructions and Bedrock/AWS prerequisites.
